articles.title: UK Football Police Unit accused of ‘bringing Hillsborough’ into alcohol debate
articles.summary: ‘The disaster was not caused by alcohol,’ says fan group. Police say they had not intended to make such a link. English football’s leading fans’ group has criticised the UK Football Policing Unit for “bringing Hillsborough into the debate” around drinking in sight of the pitch.
body: Talk of changing the law to allow fans to drink at their seat or in the stands has resurfaced after Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said the rules were outdated and discriminatory and should be scrapped.

The Football Supporters’ Association (FSA) immediately backed his call but the UKFPU urged caution, stating: “Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.”
The UKFPU added it would be “incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence”.

“The UKFPU would welcome a meeting with the prime minister to discuss his views and explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans at football games.

articles.title: Buttler injury halts England as Sri Lanka level series
articles.summary: Jos Buttler's bravery comes in vain as Sri Lanka fight back to beat England in the second one-day international at Headingley and set up a series decider at The Oval.
body: Needing 68 from 75 balls, England were cruising towards a target of 322 until Buttler retired hurt on 67 after tweaking a hamstring.
When Rehan Ahmed, Gus Atkinson and Jamie Overton fell, Buttler re-emerged with 27 now needed from 14 balls and witnessed Will Jacks fall for 52 at the non-striker's end.
England were left needing 19 from the last with Buttler on strike but, barely able to hobble a single, he holed out at deep mid-wicket. England finished on 306-9 as Sri Lanka won by 16 runs.

Buttler had earlier shown flashes of his vintage best in hitting Sri Lanka's spinners for five sixes, putting England on course after collapse of 3-14 spoiled an opening stand of 143 between Tom Banton and Ben Duckett.

articles.title: James Garner keen to live up to ‘mini-Valverde’ tag after late England call
articles.summary: Everton midfielder’s spirit and intelligence earned him another chance and he is eager to test himself against Spain in the Nations League on Saturday. “It’s a very good comparison,” James Garner says, and he is not kidding.
body: It was surely too much, despite the prefix that Tuchel attached, yet it was possible to see where he was coming from. Like Valverde, Garner wants to operate in central midfield but he can play at right-back or on the wing. And like Valverde, who they called El Pajarito – or the Little Bird – when he was a kid, Garner can sometimes fly a bit under the radar.

Is Valverde the most underrated player in the game? The more the question is asked, the more the point is lost but there is certainly something there. “You wouldn’t really call him a household name, would you?” Garner says of the Real Madrid player. “But players who have played the game – they know how good he is. I watch a lot of football. I watch all the Champions League games and he always stands out. So yeah, I would go as far as saying that he’s underrated. In my opinion, he’s one of the best midfielders in the world.”

articles.title: Former England player Andy Carroll reveals he was sexually assaulted in 2021
articles.summary: Carroll was assaulted by a man at his home while he slept. Attacker found guilty of sexual offences after player testified. The former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021.
body: Carroll revealed the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender – a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time – was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

The former Liverpool and West Ham striker, who is now a player/co-owner of the National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He then threw the man out of the house, then knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

“I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now,” wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book “at the very last minute” after discussing it with his partner, Lou Teasdale.
“Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

articles.title: Bowler Stevenson dies two months after Glasgow gold
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games bowler Mary Stevenson has died just a couple of months after winning a gold medal for Scotland at Glasgow 2026, where her winning throw earned her the moniker Mary Queen of Shots.
body: Competing just a few weeks before her 74th birthday, Stevenson became the oldest member of Team Scotland and the oldest female gold medallist in her country's history as she won the Para Mixed Pairs B2-B3 alongside Robert Barr, Sarah Jane Ewing and Jim Aitken.
Bowls Scotland stated on Facebook: "Only last weekend, she was back competing for Scotland and in great form. It is difficult to believe she is no longer with us.
"We will remember the joy of that gold medal moment and the part Mary played in it. We will also remember the character and joy she brought on and off the green.
"Our thoughts are with her family, friends, club and team-mates at this heart-breaking time."

articles.title: Leicestershire relegated by Warwickshire, subject to points appeal
articles.summary: Leicestershire are relegated, subject to an appeal against their points deduction, after being bowled out cheaply by title-chasing Warwickshire.
body: Warwickshire's march towards a ninth County Championship title continued apace at Edgbaston as relegation-bound Leicestershire became the latest to be crushed by the Bears' irrepressible bowling attack.

The visitors chose to bat in a bid to earn batting points essential to their survival hopes - but that plan went spectacularly pear-shaped as they succumbed for 125 to effectively confirm their demotion, subject to appeal.
Only Ben Cox (33) and Sol Budinger (27) resisted for long against a bang-in-form attack led by Ethan Bamber (4-42) and Chris Woakes (3-20).
The hosts then reached 130-4 by the close, with Sam Hain on 37, within reach of 1,000 runs for the season.

articles.title: Abbas & Allison shine as wickets tumble at New Road
articles.summary: Muhammad Abbas and Ben Allison take five wickets each as 20 wickets fall on day one, which ends with Worcestershire 131 ahead against Derbyshire.
body: Twenty wickets fell on a dramatic opening day at New Road that saw Worcestershire wrestle the initiative back to dismiss Derbyshire for just 88 on a fast-moving day of County Championship Division Two action.
A superb five-wicket haul from Mohammed Abbas looked to have put the visitors on top as Worcestershire were bowled out for 214.
But a resurgent Pears display, led by Ben Allison (5-22) saw the hosts charge through Derbyshire in just one session, where only Wayne Madsen (40) offered any resistance.
Nightwatchmen Allison and Fateh Singh survived the remaining three overs late on to see Worcestershire finish on 5-0, in front by 131 runs.

articles.title: UNC chancellor expected to address football investigation
articles.summary: UNC Chancellor Lee Roberts is expected to make his first public comments Thursday about the university’s investigation into the football program, including its findings and head coach Bill Belichick.
body: Roberts is scheduled to speak with reporters during a media availability at the UNC Board of Trustees meeting. He last addressed the investigation in late July, after football general manager Michael Lombardi was placed on paid administrative leave.

During the seven-week investigation, Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Bill Belichick’s son, resigned. UNC said the investigation found that “certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina’s values and standards of conduct.”
The university also said the actions were isolated and “not a systemic failure,” according to reports from WRAL.

Outside attorney Nate Huff, who led the investigation, said investigators examined allegations involving drug use and sex, as well as the program’s culture and workplace environment. The investigation included more than 60 interviews, including one with Bill Belichick.

articles.title: Hezekiah Masses and the genesis of Rob Leonard’s defense
articles.summary: While the foot injury to Darien Porter was unfortunate, it gave the Las Vegas Raiders the opportunity to reveal something they had known for the last few months. Hezekiah Masses, the fifth-round rookie cornerback out of California, would get his opportunity.
body: It would not take long for Masses to prove he was up for the challenge, securing two interceptions and being named both the AFC Defensive Player of the Week and AFC Rookie of the Week.
Many were surprised to see a rookie cornerback frustrate a quality quarterback the way Masses did Herbert, but the Raiders were hardly surprised at all.
“They’re making plays all offseason, then during training camp, so nobody was surprised at all,” said linebacker Nakobe Dean about Masses’s play.
“It’s confidence. When you’re a cornerback, it’s always great to have confidence.”

articles.title: Minnesota-Washington score predictions from Bring Me The Sports staff
articles.summary: The Gophers open Big Ten play this weekend with a tall task on the road at Washington. Current betting odds favor the Huskies by as many as 10 points. Does Minnesota have what it takes to pull off the upset? Some people seem to think so. Here are our staff writers’ predictions.
body: I fully believe that Minnesota has the personnel to go into Washington and stick with the Huskies for 60 minutes, but I’ve seen nothing from the coaching staff that makes me think that they will be put in the right positions enough to pull off the upset. The Gophers have lost five road games in a row, and that streak will continue this week.

Demond Williams is one of the most talented quarterbacks in the Big Ten, and football teams led by P.J. Fleck have struggled mightily against top-tier signal callers for the better part of the decade. I struggle to find many reasonable paths to victory for the Gophers in this one.

There’s no way in hell I’m going to pick the Gophers to lose to a team whose sideline reporter expressed significant concerns over Washington’s offensive line, running game, and whether anyone on the Huskies actually likes quarterback Demond Williams. That spells disaster, and, for once, it means the Gophers are going to win in a difficult environment. After the boat capsized in Week 2 against Mississippi State, a win in Washington will have Minnesota rowing in the right direction again.

articles.title: Trump is attending the Texas-Tennessee football game. It could cause havoc for on-field communications
articles.summary: President Donald Trump’s planned attendance at Saturday’s showdown between No. 1 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee may cause chaos by disrupting on-field communication over headsets, according to a report.
body: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said communication over headsets between coaches and players will briefly be disrupted whenever Trump moves within Neyland Stadium.

“The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium or leaves the stadium, or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication,” Sarkisian said during a news conference Thursday, according to The Athletic.
“They cut headsets to coaches. They cut headsets to coach-to-player communication. So you have to have a plan for that if and/or when, and you get no warning. So that just gets cut out,” he added.
No logistical or scheduling changes have been made regarding the team’s arrival at the stadium, Sarkisian said.

articles.title: Breetzke ton leads South Africa to 67-run ODI win over Australia
articles.summary: Matthew Breetzke scored a superb 112 to guide South Africa to a 67-run victory over Australia ‌in the first one-day international in Durban on Thursday, but the tourists will rue the loss of cheap wickets as they ‌faltered in their chase.
body: South Africa posted 297-8 in their 50 overs and Australia were well ​on course after a fast start, until poor shot selection caused their charge to collapse and they finished on 230 all out, losing ​their last nine wickets for 101 runs.

Australia will welcome the ‌likely return of captain Pat Cummins for the second match in the three-game series in Johannesburg on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, but ​if this series is a fact-finding mission ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe, there will be much food for thought.
"I'm pretty ​disappointed," Australia captain Mitch Marsh said. "South Africa outplayed us. It was ⁠a good game of cricket but we ⁠fell well short.
"We had our opportunities, I am probably going to sound like a broken record speaking about having partnerships in our ‌batting, but we weren't able to form many tonight."

articles.title: Premier League in joint call for FIFA reform amid Infantino crisis
articles.summary: The Premier League and three of its top European counterparts will on Friday issue a joint call for urgent governance reform at FIFA amid the crisis engulfing its president, Gianni Infantino.
body: Sky News can reveal that English football's top flight and the top domestic leagues in Germany, Italy and Spain will publish a collective statement demanding greater consultation on key issues such as the global football calendar.

The statement was still in the process of being formally agreed between the quartet of domestic leagues on Thursday afternoon and it was unclear whether it would specifically call for Infantino to stand down.

One football insider said: "The Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga and Serie A are going to issue a joint statement insisting that FIFA must reform to have more independent oversight and give stakeholders, including leagues, a meaningful role in decision-making."

The source said it followed a legal complaint filed nearly two years ago by the European Leagues Association - including the quartet behind Friday's planned statement - to the EU about FIFA's handling of the International Match Calendar.
